name: Lee Begins Withdrawal
desc: Following the failure of Pickett's Charge on July 3, Lee began organizing the withdrawal of the Army of Northern Virginia toward the Potomac River.

name: Fairfield
desc: Important cavalry action west of Gettysburg during the Confederate retreat. Union cavalry attempted to disrupt withdrawal routes.

name: Monterey Pass
desc: Night battle fought during a rainstorm as Union cavalry attacked Confederate wagon trains moving through the mountain pass.

name: Hagerstown
desc: Lee concentrated his army around Hagerstown while searching for a safe crossing back into Virginia.

name: Williamsport Crossing
desc: Confederate forces crossed the Potomac River after completing their withdrawal from Pennsylvania, ending the Gettysburg Campaign.

name: J.E.B. Stuart
desc: Stuart's cavalry screened Lee's retreat and protected Confederate columns moving toward the Potomac.

name: George G. Meade
desc: Meade cautiously pursued Lee following the battle, seeking opportunities to strike the retreating Confederate army.
